title: fix(app-shell): Studio names Explain access contributors and the flow trigger object by label (objectui#13056)
body:
Fixes #13056
Clause-②: no

## What changed

Two Studio surfaces now draw the label the served metadata already carries, the way the Principal card does since objectui#12693. The machine name stays on the tooltip (`title`). While a label loads, when the read fails, or when the item has no label, the machine name is the text, as before.

1. **Explain access, "Contributed by" chips** (`AccessExplainPanel.tsx`). Each layer's contributor chip now renders through the Principal card's own `CitedItemChip`. A `position` contributor takes its `meta/position` label and a `permission_set` contributor takes its `meta/permission` label. Both come from the same once-per-run, per-type list read (`lookUpItemLabels`), which now also covers the names the layers cite. The chip's `title` is the name first, then the kind and `via` it carried before (`org_member · position · via everyone`). A `system` contributor is never labelled. The Principal card's chips are unchanged: they get no `detail`, so their title is still the bare name.
2. **Flow header, Trigger pill** (`previews/FlowPreview.tsx`, `FlowMetaPills`). The trigger's object (a record trigger's `objectName`, or the object a time-relative sweep reads) now shows its label, e.g. "Record updated · Task". The label comes from `useObjectCatalog`, the read the Start node's object picker already makes (`GET /meta/object?preview=draft`), so the header and the inspector draw one label. The object name moves to the pill's `title`.

No new package export, no new prop on an exported component, and no new language-pack key.

## File surface: one line outside the dispatch list

`inspectors/ObjectPicker.tsx` gains the `export` keyword on `useObjectCatalog`, plus a doc-comment line. The ruling says the header must use "the same resolver the neighbouring surface already uses on that page", and that resolver is this module-private hook. The module stays out of every barrel, and the package entry is byte-unchanged. The claim's file surface names "the label reads they need from served metadata". The dispatch's own surface list does not name this file. This conflict is reported, not resolved silently.

## Tests

New:

- `AccessExplainPanel.contributorLabels-13056.test.tsx` (5 tests):
  - the pin (a): labelled chips;
  - a contributor the Principal card does not cite;
  - CONTROL: unlabelled and system contributors;
  - CONTROL: Principal card unchanged, plus one read per type;
  - CONTROL: a failed list.
- `previews/FlowPreview.triggerObjectLabel-13056.test.tsx` (5 tests):
  - the pin (b): record trigger shows "Task";
  - the time-relative sweep;
  - CONTROL: an unlabelled object;
  - CONTROL: a failed catalog;
  - CONTROL: a flow with no trigger.

The no-catalog readings in `FlowPreview.headerPills-11779.test.tsx` and `StudioDesignSurface.flowStatusTruth-11779.test.tsx` are unchanged and green. Neither of them serves a catalog, so they still read `task`.

Each ablation was run at HEAD `9c04f63e5a` through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which restores the file itself. Each restore is proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- **Row (a):** the contributor chip's `label=` prop was moved off (anchor 1 to 0, blob `23beb1a5e954` to `460f26ce303a`). 4 failed, 1 passed. The passing test is the failed-list control. Two controls fail too, because they wait on the label as their settle anchor. The restore matches HEAD `23beb1a5e954`.
- **Row (b):** `objectLabel` was forced to `undefined` (blob `ee897177aca4` to `89fd76fc1066`). The two label pins failed and the three controls passed. The restore matches HEAD `ee897177aca4`.

## Gates

All run on `9c04f63e5a`:

- **Targeted vitest:** 15 files, 102 tests, all passed (the touched and new files plus their neighbours).
- **Build and type-check:** the app-shell dependency closure build exited 0. `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0.
- **ESLint, narrowed to the 5 changed files:** 0 errors (JSON formatter, 5 files counted). Type-aware linting is not configured in `eslint.config.js`, so this narrowing cannot move any verdict on an untouched file. The one new warning is `react-refresh/only-export-components` on the new export.
- **The pre-tsc battery:**
  - `phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity` and `control-bytes` all exited 0.
  - `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-presence` and `check:new-line-citations` all exited 0.
  - `check:spec-floors` exited 1 with `no-artifact`, because it needs a whole-workspace build. That is recorded per the dispatch and not fixed.
- **Declared to CI:** the full `packages/app-shell/` vitest directory.

## Acceptance notes

- When the explain answer names a contributor that the principal never held, the list read covers it too (pinned).
- `FlowMetaPills` now makes one object-catalog read per mount, the same request the Start node picker makes on the same page.
